gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Samsung's 45W 'Super Fast Charging 2.0' needs a 45W adapter plus a 5A cable, or that the built-in retractable cables on these 'charger with cable' blocks top out at 3 A. On the UGREEN X605, the retractable cable's PPS range is 5–21 V at up to 3 A, and only the separate USB-C port offers 5–11 V at up to 4.5 A. ESR also rates its Xtend 45W at up to 3 A.
standout_why: Whoa Home (rank 3/4) is the only rival I could read that touches this. It says PPS is 'what a Samsung needs for Super Fast Charging', 'for 100 W the cable must be rated for 5 A', and 'A cheap cable silently limits a 140 W charger to 60 W'. It never says Samsung's 45W mode needs a 5A cable, and it never mentions built-in or retractable cables. Tom's Hardware's best-chargers page came back truncated with no body text, and Android Authority returned 403, so I could not check either one. ChatGPT's own answer says the Anker 45W is 'better for compatible Samsung phones that support 45W fast charging' but never mentions the cable rating.
decides: For a shopper with a Galaxy S22–S24 Ultra or Plus (45W-capable), every retractable 'block with cable' on our page except possibly the UGREEN 100W cuts charging to the 25W class through its built-in cable. That covers the UGREEN X605 (3 A cable), the ESR Xtend 45W (3 A max) and the Anker Nano 35W (no PPS listed, 3 A max). On the X605 they need the separate USB-C port and their own 5A cable. For a 45W Samsung phone, a block that ships with a separate cable fits better, such as the Anker Nano 45W A2692 with PPS 5–11 V at 5 A. Anker says S25+ and S25 Ultra reach Super Fast Charging with a 3A cable too, but Samsung's US page says a 3A cable 'won't work well' for 2.0, so the safe advice is a 5A cable. This does not change anything for iPhone buyers.

findings.label: PPS range on the built-in retractable cable
findings.value: 5–21 V at up to 3 A; fixed PD 60 W (20 V / 3 A max)

findings.note: Barton writes: 'Anscheinend nutzt hier UGREEN ein Kabel, das auf 3A limitiert ist' (UGREEN appears to use a cable limited to 3 A). He infers, without measuring, a ceiling of 25–30 W for Samsung phones before the S25 Ultra. I could not open ugreen.com to confirm (HTTP 429).

findings.label: PPS range on the separate USB-C port
findings.value: 5–11 V at up to 4.5 A; fixed PD 65 W (20 V / 3.25 A)
findings.source_title: UGREEN X605 Test: 65W Ladegerät mit ausziehbarem USB-C Kabel im Test (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2025-07-04)
findings.note: 11 V × 4.5 A ≈ 49.5 W, so this port can feed Samsung's 45W PPS mode, but only through a separate 5A cable. Barton loaded the port at 65 W for more than 4 hours: it passed, reached about 90 °C, and ran at 79–90% efficiency.

findings.label: Anker support: 45W label conditions
findings.value: The 'Super fast charging 2.0' label needs a 5A (100 W) USB-C cable, a 45W-capable Samsung, and a charger that follows the '9V/5A PPS protocol'. Most Anker 45W PPS chargers show only 'Super fast charging', with charge time 'nearly the same'.
findings.source_title: Why does my Samsung phone not appear "Super fast charging 2.0"? | Anker Support
findings.note: The article also says the label may not appear when several ports are in use, because each port gets less power.
